claim: Lfng-eGFP expression in the hippocampus is restricted to the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the dentate gyrus.
source: Spatially, Lfng-eGFP expression in the hippocampus was restricted to the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the dentate gyrus, where neural stem and progenitor cells reside (Seri et al., 2001) (Figure 1A, left panel).
evidence: Supported by confocal microscopy images showing eGFP expression pattern (Figure 1A) and citation to published work on NSC location.

claim: Lfng-eGFP+ cells have triangular soma located in the SGZ with a single radial process extending through the granule cell layer and ending in fine arborizations in the molecular layer.
source: Lfng-eGFP+ cells closely resembled NSCs: their triangular soma was located in the SGZ, from which a single radial process extended orthogonally and spanned the granule cell layer, ending in fine arborizations within the molecular layer (Figure 1A, right panel).
evidence: Morphological characterization based on microscopy images showing cell structure.

claim: In situ hybridization for Lfng mRNA confirms that eGFP expression recapitulates the endogenous Lfng expression pattern in the adult dentate gyrus.
source: In situ hybridization for Lfng mRNA confirmed that eGFP expression recapitulated the endogenous Lfng expression pattern in the adult dentate gyrus (Figure 1B).
evidence: In situ hybridization data showing mRNA expression pattern matching eGFP reporter.

claim: In LfngTm1Grid; Lfng-eGFP mice, β-Gal and eGFP co-localize, demonstrating that the regulatory elements driving eGFP expression are active in the same cells that express β-Gal.
source: In the resulting LfngTm1Grid; Lfng-eGFP mice, β-Gal and eGFP co-localized (Figure 1C), demonstrating that the regulatory elements driving eGFP expression in Lfng-eGFP mice are active in the same cells that expressed β-Gal in LfngTm1Grid mice.
evidence: Co-localization data from double transgenic mice showing overlap of two reporter systems.

claim: Nestin, Sox2, Vimentin, and GFAP are all expressed in Lfng-eGFP+ cells.
source: Finally, Nestin, Sox2, Vimentin, and GFAP, known to label NSCs, were all expressed in Lfng-eGFP+ cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing co-expression of known NSC markers with eGFP.

claim: eGFP is cleared from Lfng-eGFP+ ANPs between days 1 and 3 following a single dose of BrdU.
source: eGFP was cleared from Lfng-eGFP+ ANPs, but not from Nestin-GFP+ (Mignone et al., 2004) ANPs, between days 1 and 3 (Figure 1E, left graph).
evidence: BrdU pulse-chase experiment showing temporal dynamics of eGFP expression in ANPs.

claim: The clearance of eGFP from ANPs correlates with the half-life of GFP.
source: The clearance correlates with the half-life of GFP (Corish and Tyler-Smith, 1999), suggesting that the eGFP in ANPs is likely from the protein retained by the first progeny of Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs.
evidence: Inference based on known GFP protein half-life from cited literature.

claim: Only 10% of Type 2a cells (Sox2+ early ANPs) are eGFP+ in Lfng-eGFP mice compared to almost 95% in Nestin-GFP mice.
source: Indeed, only 10% of Type 2a cells (Sox2+ early ANPs) were eGFP+ in Lfng-eGFP mice compared to almost 95% in Nestin-GFP mice (Figure 1E, right graph).
evidence: Quantitative comparison of marker expression between two transgenic mouse lines.

claim: No Type 2b cells (late ANPs) express Lfng-eGFP.
source: No Type 2b cells (late ANPs) expressed Lfng-eGFP (Figure 1E, right panel).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing absence of eGFP in Tbr2+ late ANPs.

claim: Lfng-eGFP is not detected in neuroblasts/immature neurons, granule cells, or astrocytes.
source: Lfng-eGFP was not detected in neuroblasts/immature neurons, granule cells, or astrocytes (Figure 1F).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing lack of co-localization with differentiated cell markers.

claim: In Lfng-eGFP mice, 81.7 ± 2.6% of eGFP+ cells are NSCs, 16.4 ± 1.5% are ANPs, and 1.9 ± 1.1% are other cell types.
source: The overall quantification of the cell-type expression of eGFP indicated that the majority of eGFP+ cells in Lfng-eGFP mice were NSCs (81.7 ± 2.6%), while only 16.4 ± 1.5% were ANPs and 1.9 ± 1.1% were other cell types (Figure 1G).
evidence: Quantitative stereological analysis of cell type distribution.

claim: In Nestin-GFP mice, 36.1 ± 3.7% of GFP+ cells are ANPs, 33.7 ± 2.8% are other cell types, and 30.2 ± 2.4% are NSCs.
source: In contrast, in Nestin-GFP mice, the majority of GFP+ cells were ANPs (36.1 ± 3.7%), followed by other cell types (33.7 ± 2.8%) and NSCs (30.2 ± 2.4%).
evidence: Quantitative stereological analysis comparing cell type distribution in different transgenic line.

claim: Only 15.0 ± 3.0% of eGFP+ cells were lost in Lfng-eGFP mice following temozolomide treatment.
source: Indeed, only 15.0 ± 3.0% of the eGFP+ cells were lost in Lfng-eGFP mice following temozolomide treatment (N = 4, p=0.27), compared to 35.0 ± 4.0% in the Nestin-GFP mice (N = 4, p=0.0035).
evidence: Experimental data from temozolomide treatment showing differential cell loss between mouse lines.

claim: 35.0 ± 4.0% of GFP+ cells were lost in Nestin-GFP mice following temozolomide treatment.
source: Indeed, only 15.0 ± 3.0% of the eGFP+ cells were lost in Lfng-eGFP mice following temozolomide treatment (N = 4, p=0.27), compared to 35.0 ± 4.0% in the Nestin-GFP mice (N = 4, p=0.0035).
evidence: Experimental data from temozolomide treatment showing cell loss.

claim: Electroconvulsive shock (ECS) activates Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs.
source: A robust increase in the percentage of BrdU+ Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs in both conditions (N = 4 per group in ECS, p=0.0006; and N = 6 per group in PE, p=0.0271) indicated that Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs are plastic, as expected (Figure 2B).
evidence: BrdU incorporation data showing increased NSC division following ECS treatment.

claim: Physical exercise activates Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs.
source: A robust increase in the percentage of BrdU+ Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs in both conditions (N = 4 per group in ECS, p=0.0006; and N = 6 per group in PE, p=0.0271) indicated that Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs are plastic, as expected (Figure 2B).
evidence: BrdU incorporation data showing increased NSC division following physical exercise.

claim: Over the course of 30 days, the total number of BrdU+ cells in the dentate gyrus follows the same pattern of decline in both Lfng-eGFP and Nestin-GFP mice (R = 0.9992).
source: Over the course of 30 days, the total number of BrdU+ cells in the dentate gyrus followed the same pattern of decline (R = 0.9992; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Longitudinal BrdU tracking data showing correlation between two mouse models.

claim: The number of Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs declines over an 18 month period comparably to the number of Nestin-GFP+ NSCs.
source: The number of Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs declines over an 18 month period comparably to the number of Nestin-GFP+ NSCs (left panel; N = 4 per timepoint per genotype).
evidence: Longitudinal quantification of NSC numbers during aging in two mouse models.

claim: Lfng-eGFP remains selective for NSCs during aging (p>0.15 for all timepoints).
source: While Lfng-eGFP remains selective for NSCs during aging (p>0.15 for all timepoints, Tukey post-hoc test), Nestin-GFP labels significantly more non-neuroprogenitors in older mice (p<0.002; Tukey post-hoc test).
evidence: Statistical analysis of cell type specificity across aging timepoints.

claim: Nestin-GFP labels significantly more non-neuroprogenitors in older mice (p<0.002).
source: While Lfng-eGFP remains selective for NSCs during aging (p>0.15 for all timepoints, Tukey post-hoc test), Nestin-GFP labels significantly more non-neuroprogenitors in older mice (p<0.002; Tukey post-hoc test).
evidence: Statistical analysis showing decreased specificity of Nestin-GFP during aging.

claim: In Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT;Lfng-eGFP triple transgenic mice, 89.1 ± 4.0% of tdTomato+ cells are eGFP+ one day following induction.
source: One day following induction, 89.1 ± 4.0% of tdTomato+ cells were eGFP+ and 37.9 ± 1.5% of Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs were tdTomato+ (Figure 3B).
evidence: Quantification of co-expression in triple transgenic mice after tamoxifen induction.

claim: 37.9 ± 1.5% of Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs are tdTomato+ one day following induction in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT;Lfng-eGFP mice.
source: One day following induction, 89.1 ± 4.0% of tdTomato+ cells were eGFP+ and 37.9 ± 1.5% of Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs were tdTomato+ (Figure 3B).
evidence: Quantification of recombination efficiency in NSCs after tamoxifen induction.

claim: No tdTomato expression is observed after vehicle administration in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice.
source: No tdTomato expression was observed after vehicle administration (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Control experiment showing no leaky expression without tamoxifen.

claim: Fifteen days following induction of DTR in Lfng-CreERT2; iDTR mice and activation by diphtheria toxin, there is a 36.8 ± 1.5% reduction in NSCs (p=0.0244).
source: Fifteen days following induction of DTR in Lfng-CreERT2; iDTR mice and activation by diphtheria toxin, we observed a significant reduction in both NSCs (36.8 ± 1.5%; N = 3–4 per group; p=0.0244) and the Ki67+ cells (57.3 ± 2.4%; p<0.0001) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Diphtheria toxin ablation experiment showing NSC depletion.

claim: Fifteen days following induction of DTR in Lfng-CreERT2; iDTR mice and activation by diphtheria toxin, there is a 57.3 ± 2.4% reduction in Ki67+ cells (p<0.0001).
source: Fifteen days following induction of DTR in Lfng-CreERT2; iDTR mice and activation by diphtheria toxin, we observed a significant reduction in both NSCs (36.8 ± 1.5%; N = 3–4 per group; p=0.0244) and the Ki67+ cells (57.3 ± 2.4%; p<0.0001) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Diphtheria toxin ablation experiment showing reduction in cycling cells.

claim: Induced NSCs in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice divide both asymmetrically to give rise to ANPs and symmetrically to give rise to two Sox2+ cells with prominent GFAP+ radial processes.
source: They divided both asymmetrically, to give rise to ANPs (Figure 3C, middle panel) and symmetrically, to give rise to two Sox2+ cells connected via cytoplasm and both having prominent GFAP+ radial processes (Figure 3C, right panel).
evidence: Microscopy images showing different division modes of labeled NSCs.

claim: Within 3 days of induction in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice, tdTomato+ Tbr2+ late ANPs (Type 2b cells) are detected.
source: Within 3 days of induction we detected tdTomato+ Tbr2+ late ANPs (Type 2b cells), followed by Dcx+ immature neurons 7 days after (Figure 3D).
evidence: Temporal lineage tracing showing appearance of late ANPs.

claim: Dcx+ immature neurons are detected 7 days after induction in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice.
source: Within 3 days of induction we detected tdTomato+ Tbr2+ late ANPs (Type 2b cells), followed by Dcx+ immature neurons 7 days after (Figure 3D).
evidence: Temporal lineage tracing showing appearance of immature neurons.

claim: Thirty days following induction in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice, tdTomato+ cells express the granule cell marker NeuN.
source: Thirty days following induction, tdTomato+ cells expressed the granule cell marker NeuN (Figure 3D) and had extended processes reaching the molecular layer, prominent dendritic spines, and an axon extending throughout the hilus to the CA3 region (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Lineage tracing showing mature neuronal differentiation with morphological features.

claim: tdTomato+ S100β+ astrocytes are detected in the granule cell layer in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice.
source: In addition to neuronal progeny, we also detected tdTomato+ S100β+ astrocytes in the granule cell layer (Figure 3E, left panel) and tdTomato+ Sox2+ GFAP+ astrocyte-like cells in the hilus (Figure 3E, right panel).
evidence: Lineage tracing showing astrocytic differentiation.

claim: tdTomato+ Sox2+ GFAP+ astrocyte-like cells are detected in the hilus in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice.
source: In addition to neuronal progeny, we also detected tdTomato+ S100β+ astrocytes in the granule cell layer (Figure 3E, left panel) and tdTomato+ Sox2+ GFAP+ astrocyte-like cells in the hilus (Figure 3E, right panel).
evidence: Lineage tracing showing astrocyte-like cell differentiation.

claim: NSCs form the majority (85.7% ± 0.9) of induced cells at 1 day post-induction in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice.
source: Initially, most of the population consisted of NSCs with some ANPs and astrocyte-like cells (GFAP+, S100β-).
evidence: Quantitative fate mapping data at early timepoint after induction.

claim: The population of ANPs and immature neurons remains stable from 15 days on in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice.
source: Interestingly, the population of ANPs and immature neurons remained stable from 15 days on, indicating a continuous replenishment of these cell types.
evidence: Longitudinal quantification showing stable cell populations over time.

claim: The granule cell number steadily increases from 15 days on and represents about 30% of all tdTomato+ cells at 60 days following induction in Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice.
source: The granule cell number steadily increased from 15 days on and represented about 30% of all tdTomato+ cells at 60 days following induction.
evidence: Longitudinal quantification showing accumulation of mature neurons.

claim: Notch1 is expressed on the surface of NSCs.
source: In agreement with published data (Breunig et al., 2007; Lavado et al., 2010), we found the key elements of the Notch pathway expressed in the NSCs and surrounding progeny: Notch1 on the surface of NSCs, Jag1 on presumed ANPs surrounding NSCs, and Dll1 on granule neurons neighboring the apical parts of the NSC soma (Figure 4A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing Notch1 localization, supported by citations.

claim: Jag1 is expressed on presumed ANPs surrounding NSCs.
source: In agreement with published data (Breunig et al., 2007; Lavado et al., 2010), we found the key elements of the Notch pathway expressed in the NSCs and surrounding progeny: Notch1 on the surface of NSCs, Jag1 on presumed ANPs surrounding NSCs, and Dll1 on granule neurons neighboring the apical parts of the NSC soma (Figure 4A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing Jag1 localization, supported by citations.

claim: Dll1 is expressed on granule neurons neighboring the apical parts of the NSC soma.
source: In agreement with published data (Breunig et al., 2007; Lavado et al., 2010), we found the key elements of the Notch pathway expressed in the NSCs and surrounding progeny: Notch1 on the surface of NSCs, Jag1 on presumed ANPs surrounding NSCs, and Dll1 on granule neurons neighboring the apical parts of the NSC soma (Figure 4A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing Dll1 localization, supported by citations.

claim: Hes5 is present in some but not all Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs.
source: In addition, Hes5 (an indicator of canonical Notch pathway; Imayoshi et al., 2010; Lugert et al., 2010) was present in some but not all Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing heterogeneous Hes5 expression, with citations supporting Hes5 as Notch indicator.

claim: Approximately half of the NSCs have active Venus+ Notch signaling at any given time in CBF:H2B-Venus mice.
source: Approximately half of the NSCs had active Venus+ Notch signaling at any given time, whereas Venus expression declined in early (Sox2+) and late (Tbr2+) ANPs as well as in neuroblasts and immature neurons (Dcx+) (Figure 4B).
evidence: Quantification of Venus reporter expression in NSCs using Notch reporter mice.

claim: Venus expression declines in early (Sox2+) and late (Tbr2+) ANPs as well as in neuroblasts and immature neurons (Dcx+) in CBF:H2B-Venus mice.
source: Approximately half of the NSCs had active Venus+ Notch signaling at any given time, whereas Venus expression declined in early (Sox2+) and late (Tbr2+) ANPs as well as in neuroblasts and immature neurons (Dcx+) (Figure 4B).
evidence: Quantification of Venus reporter expression showing downregulation during differentiation.

claim: Most NeuN+ cells are positive for Venus signal with various degrees of intensity in CBF:H2B-Venus mice.
source: Notch signaling was turned on again in mature granule neurons as most of the NeuN+ cells were positive for Venus signal with various degrees of intensity (Figure 4B), in agreement with the previous reports (Brandt et al., 2010; Breunig et al., 2007).
evidence: Quantification of Venus expression in mature neurons, supported by citations.

claim: Over 90% of Venus+ cells in the SGZ express NICD1 in CBF:H2B-Venus mice.
source: Indeed, the NICD1 expression overlapped with Venus expression in CBF:H2B-Venus mice: over 90% in SGZ and over 95% in GZ (Figure 4C).
evidence: Co-localization quantification validating NICD1 as marker of Notch activity.

claim: Over 95% of Venus+ cells in the GZ express NICD1 in CBF:H2B-Venus mice.
source: Indeed, the NICD1 expression overlapped with Venus expression in CBF:H2B-Venus mice: over 90% in SGZ and over 95% in GZ (Figure 4C).
evidence: Co-localization quantification validating NICD1 as marker of Notch activity.

claim: Mice lacking Lfng have markedly fewer NSCs than wild-type mice.
source: Mice lacking Lfng had markedly fewer NSCs than wild-type mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: Quantification of NSC numbers in constitutive knockout mice.

claim: NSCs lacking Lfng are cycling (Ki67+) in significantly higher proportions than wild-type NSCs (p=0.0221).
source: We examined the ratio of cycling Ki67+ NSCs and BrdU+ NSCs in mutant and wild-type mice and found that NSCs lacking Lfng were both cycling (Figure 5C, left panel) and in S-phase (Figure 5C, middle panel) in significantly higher proportions than wild-type NSCs (N = 4; p=0.0221 for Ki67+ NSCs; p=0.0017 for BrdU+ NSCs).
evidence: Quantification of cell cycle markers in knockout versus wild-type mice.

claim: NSCs lacking Lfng are in S-phase (BrdU+) in significantly higher proportions than wild-type NSCs (p=0.0017).
source: We examined the ratio of cycling Ki67+ NSCs and BrdU+ NSCs in mutant and wild-type mice and found that NSCs lacking Lfng were both cycling (Figure 5C, left panel) and in S-phase (Figure 5C, middle panel) in significantly higher proportions than wild-type NSCs (N = 4; p=0.0221 for Ki67+ NSCs; p=0.0017 for BrdU+ NSCs).
evidence: Quantification of S-phase entry in knockout versus wild-type mice.

claim: Considerably more mutant NSCs are in S-phase than either wild-type NSC clones or NSCs in control mice in iLfngfl/fl conditional knockout mice.
source: Considerably more mutant NSCs were in S-phase than were either wild-type NSC clones or NSCs in control mice (Figure 5C, right panel).
evidence: Quantification of BrdU incorporation in conditional knockout clones versus controls.

claim: iLfngfl/fl wild-type clones have a similar ratio of BrdU+ NSCs as control mice.
source: Interestingly, iLfngfl/fl wild-type clones had a similar ratio of BrdU+ NSCs as control mice (Figure 5C, right panel), suggesting that the effect of Lfng in NSCs is cell-autonomous.
evidence: Comparison of BrdU incorporation between non-recombined clones and controls, leading to inference about cell autonomy.

claim: When Lfng−/+ mice are subjected to ECS, they have a significantly higher ratio of BrdU+ NSCs than observed in either sham Lfng−/+ control (p=0.0178) or ECS-treated Lfng-eGFP mice.
source: This effect persists not only in physiological but also in pathological conditions: when Lfng−/+ mice were subjected to ECS, they had a significantly higher ratio of BrdU+ NSCs than observed in either sham Lfng−/+ control (N = 3–4, p=0.0178; Figure 5D) or ECS-treated Lfng-eGFP mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: Comparison of ECS response in knockout versus control mice.

claim: Notch signaling, as measured by NICD1 immunofluorescence intensity, is much lower in individual mutant NSC clones in iLfngfl/fl mice two weeks after induction compared to controls.
source: Indeed, Notch signaling, as measured by NICD1 immunofluorescence intensity, was much lower in individual mutant NSC clones in iLfngfl/fl mice two weeks after induction compared to controls (Figure 5E).
evidence: Quantification of NICD1 intensity in mutant versus control NSCs.

claim: Many double-labeled NSCs (CldU/IdU) are observed in wild-type mice at 3 and 7 days, but only a few are detected in Lfng−/+ mice at either timepoint, and none are found in iLfngfl/fl mice.
source: Many double-labeled NSCs were observed in the wild-type mice, only a few were detected in the Lfng−/+ mice at either timepoint, but none were found in iLfngfl/fl mice (Figure 5F).
evidence: Sequential thymidine analog labeling showing differences in cell cycle re-entry.

claim: Lfng−/+ mice have a decreased ratio of CldU/Ki67 double labeled NSCs 7 days following CldU injection (p=0.0105).
source: As Lfng−/+ mice had a decreased ratio of CldU/Ki67 double labeled NSCs 7 days following CldU injection (N = 4; p=0.0105; Figure 5G), these data strongly indicate that Lfng mutant NSCs either dilute BrdU by multiple divisions, die, or directly differentiate/ transform into another cell type over the course of seven days.
evidence: Quantification of cycling NSCs retaining label, leading to inference about cell fate.

claim: In Lfng mutant mice, after a two-hour pulse, only 5.2% of the initial BrdU+ NSC population retains BrdU after 7 days (p=0.0003).
source: In Lfng mutant mice, after a two-hour pulse, only 5.2% of the initial BrdU+ NSC population retained BrdU after 7 days (N = 4 per timepoint, p=0.0003).
evidence: BrdU retention assay showing loss of label in mutant NSCs.

claim: In control mice, 92.4% of the initial BrdU+ NSC population retains BrdU after 7 days (p=0.38).
source: In control mice, however, 92.4% of the initial BrdU+ NSC population retained BrdU after 7 days (N = 4 per timepoint, p=0.38).
evidence: BrdU retention assay showing maintenance of label in control NSCs.

claim: iLfngfl/fl mice have fewer apoptotic cells than control mice.
source: Both immunostaining for activated caspase-3 and the ApopTag assay, which detects DNA strand breaks, indicated that iLfngfl/fl actually had fewer apoptotic cells than control (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Apoptosis detection assays showing reduced cell death in mutants.

claim: There is a declining trend in the number of mutant NSCs at 1, 7, and 30 days post-induction in iLfngfl/fl mice (p=0.8215; 0.11; 0.06 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively).
source: We observed a declining trend in the number of mutant NSCs (p=0.8215; 0.11; 0.06 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively), and a significant decline in the number of mutant ANPs (p=0.2817; 0.0024; 0.0049 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively) (Figure 5H, middle panel).
evidence: Longitudinal quantification of cell populations in conditional knockout.

claim: There is a significant decline in the number of mutant ANPs at 7 and 30 days post-induction in iLfngfl/fl mice (p=0.0024; 0.0049 for 7 and 30 days, respectively).
source: We observed a declining trend in the number of mutant NSCs (p=0.8215; 0.11; 0.06 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively), and a significant decline in the number of mutant ANPs (p=0.2817; 0.0024; 0.0049 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively) (Figure 5H, middle panel).
evidence: Longitudinal quantification showing reduced ANP production in mutants.

claim: There is a notable increase in tdTomato+ astrocyte-like cells at 7 and 30 days post-induction in iLfngfl/fl mice (p=0.0003 and p<0.0001, respectively).
source: Interestingly, we observed a notable increase in tdTomato+ astrocyte-like cells at 7 and 30 days post-induction (p=0.0003 and p<0.0001, respectively).
evidence: Quantification showing increased astrocytic differentiation in mutants.

claim: A greater number of BrdU-retaining astrocyte-like cells are found in Lfng mutant mice at 7 days (p=0.0302) but not at 30 days (p=0.4412).
source: we quantified the BrdU-retaining astrocyte-like cells and found a greater number of these cells in Lfng mutant mice, but only at 7 days (N = 4 per group, p=0.0302; Figure 5H, right panel). At 30 days, there was no difference compared to control mice (p=0.4412), suggesting that NSCs lacking Lfng differentiate more rapidly into astrocyte-like cells, depleting the NSC population more quickly.
evidence: BrdU retention assay showing temporal dynamics of astrocytic differentiation, leading to inference about differentiation rate.

claim: Mice lacking Dll1 have far fewer NSCs than wild-type mice or those lacking Jag1.
source: Mice lacking Dll1 (Dll1tm1Gos (JAX 002957; Dll1−/+)) (Hrabĕĕ de Angelis et al., 1997) had far fewer NSCs than wild-type mice or those lacking Jag1 (Jag1tm1Grid (JAX 010616; Jag1−/+)) (Xue et al., 1999) or Lfng (Figure 6A, Figure 5B, respectively).
evidence: Quantification of NSC numbers in Dll1 knockout mice compared to other genotypes, with citations.

claim: Dll1−/+ mice have a substantial increase in the ratio of cycling Ki67+ cells (p=0.0007) and BrdU+ NSCs (p<0.0001).
source: This was accompanied by a substantial increase in the ratio of cycling, Ki67+ cells and BrdU+ NSCs (N = 4 per group; p=0.0007 for Ki67, p<0.0001 for BrdU experiment; Figure 6B), suggesting that the dramatic decrease in the NSC population in mice lacking Dll1 might be due to increased cycling and S-phase entry, as observed in Lfng−/+ mice.
evidence: Quantification of cell cycle markers in Dll1 knockout, leading to inference about mechanism.

claim: No difference in the amount of NSCs is observed between wild-type and Jag1−/+ mice (p=0.1663).
source: Interestingly, no difference in the amount of NSCs was observed between wild-type and Jag1−/+ mice (N = 4 per group; p=0.1663; Figure 6A), but there was an upward trend in the proportion of BrdU+ NSCs (N = 4 per group; p=0.8393; Figure 6B, middle panel).
evidence: Quantification showing no change in total NSC numbers in Jag1 knockout.

claim: There is a significant increase in Ki67+ NSCs lacking Jag1 (p<0.0001).
source: There was, however, a significant increase in Ki67+ NSCs lacking Jag1 (N = 4 per group, p<0.0001; Figure 6B, left panel), suggesting that these NSCs may have a prolonged cell cycle.
evidence: Quantification of cycling NSCs in Jag1 knockout, leading to inference about cell cycle duration.

claim: The ratio of BrdU+ NSCs is significantly higher in iJag1fl/fl mice compared to controls (p=0.0028).
source: In these conditional homozygous knockout mice (iJag1fl/fl), the ratio of BrdU+ mutant NSCs was significantly higher than in controls (Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT; N = 4 per group, p=0.0028; Figure 6B, right panel).
evidence: Quantification of S-phase entry in conditional Jag1 knockout.

claim: The number of CldU/IdU double-labeled NSCs in both Jag1−/+ and iJag1fl/fl mice is notably higher than controls at both 3 and 7 days (p=0.0164 at 3d, p=0.0016 at 7d; p=0.0003 for iJag1fl/fl mice).
source: The number of CldU/IdU double-labeled NSCs in both Jag1−/+ and iJag1fl/fl mice was notably higher than controls at both 3 and 7 days (N = 4 per group, p=0.0164 at 3d, p=0.0016 at 7d; p=0.0003 for iJag1fl/fl mice; Figure 6C) and accompanied by a greater proportion of CldU+ Ki67+ NSCs (N = 4 per group; p=0.005 for wild-type vs Jag1−/+; Figure 6D).
evidence: Sequential thymidine analog labeling showing increased cell cycle re-entry in Jag1 mutants.

claim: There is a greater proportion of CldU+ Ki67+ NSCs in Jag1−/+ mice compared to wild-type (p=0.005).
source: The number of CldU/IdU double-labeled NSCs in both Jag1−/+ and iJag1fl/fl mice was notably higher than controls at both 3 and 7 days (N = 4 per group, p=0.0164 at 3d, p=0.0016 at 7d; p=0.0003 for iJag1fl/fl mice; Figure 6C) and accompanied by a greater proportion of CldU+ Ki67+ NSCs (N = 4 per group; p=0.005 for wild-type vs Jag1−/+; Figure 6D).
evidence: Quantification of cycling NSCs retaining label in Jag1 knockout.

claim: NICD1 expression is higher in individual mutant NSC clones in iJag1fl/fl mice two weeks after induction compared to controls.
source: The increase in NICD1 expression in individual mutant NSC clones in iJag1fl/fl mice two weeks after induction (Figure 6E) supports this notion, in agreement with the reported conditional overexpression of NICD1, which increases cell cycle re-entry of NSCs (Breunig et al., 2007).
evidence: Quantification of NICD1 intensity in Jag1 mutant NSCs, supported by citation.

claim: There is no difference in double-labeled NSCs between Dll1−/+ and wild-type mice at 3 days (p=0.9624), but at 7 days no CldU/IdU double-positive cells can be detected (p=0.0016).
source: Conversely, there was no difference in double-labeled NSCs between Dll1−/+ and wild-type mice at 3 days, but at 7 days no CldU/IdU double-positive cells could be detected, suggesting that NSCs did not re-enter cell cycle (N = 4 per group, p=0.9624 at 3d, p=0.0016 at 7d; Figure 6C).
evidence: Sequential thymidine analog labeling showing lack of cell cycle re-entry in Dll1 mutants, leading to inference.

claim: In the absence of Dll1, none of the BrdU+ NSCs two hours following a single BrdU injection retain BrdU at 7 days.
source: In the absence of Dll1, none of the BrdU+ NSCs two hours following a single BrdU injection retained BrdU at 7 days (N = 4; Figure 6F).
evidence: BrdU retention assay showing complete loss of label in Dll1 mutant NSCs.

claim: Dll1−/+ mice have significantly more S100β+ astrocytes among BrdU+ cells 30 days after BrdU injection (p=0.016).
source: To determine the fate of NSCs in Dll1−/+ mice, we injected BrdU and sacrificed the animals 30 days later. We observed significantly more S100β+ astrocytes among the BrdU+ cells. Thus, as in Lfng−/+, more Dll1 mutant NSCs terminally differentiate into astrocytes (N = 4 per group, p=0.016; Figure 6H).
evidence: BrdU fate mapping showing increased astrocytic differentiation in Dll1 mutants.

claim: The number of BrdU retaining NSCs in Jag1−/+ mice is much greater 7 days following the BrdU pulse (1.6 fold, p=0.0028) than two hours after the pulse.
source: The findings were opposite in mice lacking Jag1: the number of BrdU retaining NSCs was much greater 7 days following the BrdU pulse (1.6 fold, p=0.0028) than two hours after the pulse (Figure 6F).
evidence: BrdU retention assay showing increased label retention in Jag1 mutants, suggesting self-renewal.

claim: The number of tdTomato+ NSCs markedly increases at both 7 and 30 days in iJag1fl/fl mutant mice compared to control mice (p=0.0263 and p<0.0001 for NSC at 7d and 30d).
source: Initially, both control and mutant mice had a similar number of tdTomato+ NSCs and ANPs, but this number markedly increased at both 7 and 30 days in mutant compared to control mice (N = 4 per group, p=0.0263 and p<0.0001 for NSC at 7d and 30d, p=0.0033 and p=0.069 for ANP at 7d and 30d; Figure 6I).
evidence: Longitudinal quantification showing NSC accumulation in Jag1 conditional knockout.

claim: The number of tdTomato+ ANPs increases at 7 days (p=0.0033) in iJag1fl/fl mutant mice compared to control mice.
source: Initially, both control and mutant mice had a similar number of tdTomato+ NSCs and ANPs, but this number markedly increased at both 7 and 30 days in mutant compared to control mice (N = 4 per group, p=0.0263 and p<0.0001 for NSC at 7d and 30d, p=0.0033 and p=0.069 for ANP at 7d and 30d; Figure 6I).
evidence: Longitudinal quantification showing ANP accumulation in Jag1 conditional knockout.

claim: Both the number of Type 2a ANPs and the size of the ANP clusters are significantly greater in Jag1−/+ mice than controls.
source: Indeed, both the number of Type 2a ANPs and the size of the ANP clusters were significantly greater in Jag1−/+ mice than controls (Figure 6G).
evidence: Quantification of ANP numbers and cluster sizes in Jag1 knockout.

claim: iJag1fl/fl mice have a prominent decrease in the number of apoptotic cells compared to wild-type.
source: To determine whether apoptosis had any role in the increased number of ANPs in Jag1 mutants, we quantified the number of apoptotic cells using activated caspase-3 staining and ApopTag. Both methods demonstrated a prominent decrease in the number of apoptotic cells in iJag1fl/fl mice compared to wild-type (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Apoptosis detection assays showing reduced cell death in Jag1 mutants.

claim: Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ double knockout mice have far fewer NSCs than wild-type (p<0.0001).
source: Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ double knockout mice had far fewer NSCs than wild-type (N = 3 for Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ and N = 4 controls; p<0.0001 for wild-type vs Lfng−/+ and Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+), but did not differ significantly from Lfng−/+ mice (N = 3 for Lfng−/+, p=0.6869 for Lfng−/+ vs Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Quantification of NSC numbers in double knockout mice.

claim: Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ double knockout mice show a higher BrdU+ NSC ratio than wild-type (p=0.0003).
source: The double knockout showed a higher BrdU+ NSC ratio than wild-type (N = 3; p=0.0001 for wild-type vs Lfng−/+, p=0.0003 for wild-type vs Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+, p=0.6724 for Lfng−/+ vs Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+; Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), similar to Lfng−/+ mice.
evidence: Quantification of S-phase entry in double knockout mice.

claim: Greater NSC cell cycle re-entry is observed in Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ double knockout mice (p<0.00001).
source: Finally, we observed greater NSC cell cycle re-entry in double knockout mice (N = 3; p<0.00001 for wild-type vs Lfng-/+; Jag1−/+ and Lfng−/+ vs Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+), suggesting that removal of Jag1 can reverse the low cell cycle re-entry phenotype observed in the NSCs lacking Lfng (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Sequential thymidine analog labeling in double knockout showing epistatic relationship.

claim: Lfng glycosylation of Notch does not affect Jag1 binding, but the NICD is not cleaved from the Jag1-Notch complex.
source: In the Notch signal-receiving NSC, Lfng glycosylation of the Notch receptor potentiates Notch signaling from Dll1 and attenuates signaling from Jag1: even though Lfng glycosylation of Notch does not affect Jag1 binding, the NICD is not cleaved from the Jag1-Notch complex.
evidence: Mechanistic explanation based on established knowledge of Lfng function.

claim: Lfng modification of Notch elevates NICD production upon Dll1 binding.
source: Lfng N-glycosylates Notch receptors (Moloney et al., 2000), affecting the intracellular cleavage of the heterodimeric receptor complex and generation of the NICD following ligand binding: typically, Lfng modification of Notch elevates NICD production upon Dll1 binding, but decreases it following engagement to Jag1 (Haines and Irvine, 2003; LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: Mechanistic explanation supported by multiple citations.

claim: Lfng modification of Notch decreases NICD production following engagement to Jag1.
source: Lfng N-glycosylates Notch receptors (Moloney et al., 2000), affecting the intracellular cleavage of the heterodimeric receptor complex and generation of the NICD following ligand binding: typically, Lfng modification of Notch elevates NICD production upon Dll1 binding, but decreases it following engagement to Jag1 (Haines and Irvine, 2003; LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: Mechanistic explanation supported by multiple citations.

claim: Notch signaling plays a key role in the balance between quiescence and activation of hippocampal neural stem cells.
source: Hippocampal neural stem cells (NSCs) integrate inputs from multiple sources to balance quiescence and activation. Notch signaling plays a key role during this process.
evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by experimental data throughout manuscript.

claim: Lunatic fringe (Lfng) is selectively expressed in NSCs.
source: Here, we report that Lunatic fringe (Lfng), a key modifier of the Notch receptor, is selectively expressed in NSCs.
evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by expression data throughout manuscript.

claim: Lfng in NSCs and Notch ligands Delta1 and Jagged1, expressed by their progeny, together influence NSC recruitment, cell cycle duration, and terminal fate.
source: Further, Lfng in NSCs and Notch ligands Delta1 and Jagged1, expressed by their progeny, together influence NSC recruitment, cell cycle duration, and terminal fate.
evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by loss-of-function experiments throughout manuscript.

claim: Lfng-mediated Notch signaling enables direct communication between a NSC and its descendants, so that progeny can send feedback signals to the 'mother' cell to modify its cell cycle status.
source: We propose a new model in which Lfng-mediated Notch signaling enables direct communication between a NSC and its descendants, so that progeny can send feedback signals to the 'mother' cell to modify its cell cycle status.
evidence: Model proposed based on integration of expression patterns and loss-of-function data.

claim: Nearly 80% of the newborn progeny of NSCs die by apoptosis.
source: Taking into account that nearly 80% of the newborn progeny of NSCs die by apoptosis (Sierra et al., 2010), the neurogenic niche needs to ensure not only that it responds properly to stimuli but also that NSCs, once they are activated, are cycling enough to produce sufficient progeny.
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published work.

claim: Communication between 'mother' and 'daughter' cells is known to regulate lateral inhibition in the vertebral neural tube.
source: Communication between 'mother' and 'daughter' cells is known to regulate lateral inhibition in the vertebral neural tube (Nikolaou et al., 2009) and Drosophila oocytes (Zhao et al., 2000), and it occurs during angiogenesis (Benedito et al., 2009) and oncogenesis (Xu et al., 2012); in each case this communication involves Notch signaling (Haines and Irvine, 2003; LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: Statement supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Communication between 'mother' and 'daughter' cells occurs during angiogenesis and oncogenesis, involving Notch signaling.
source: Communication between 'mother' and 'daughter' cells is known to regulate lateral inhibition in the vertebral neural tube (Nikolaou et al., 2009) and Drosophila oocytes (Zhao et al., 2000), and it occurs during angiogenesis (Benedito et al., 2009) and oncogenesis (Xu et al., 2012); in each case this communication involves Notch signaling (Haines and Irvine, 2003; LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: Statement supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: In the fetal brain, Notch activity maintains embryonic NSCs in an undifferentiated state by suppressing pro-neural gene expression.
source: In the fetal brain, Notch activity maintains embryonic NSCs in an undifferentiated state (Louvi and Artavanis-Tsakonas, 2006) by suppressing pro-neural gene expression (Gaiano et al., 2000; Ishibashi et al., 1994; Lütolf et al., 2002) and supporting progenitor survival (Androutsellis-Theotokis et al., 2006; Louvi and Artavanis-Tsakonas, 2006).
evidence: Statement about developmental role of Notch supported by multiple citations.

claim: In the adult brain, Notch influences quiescence, cycling, and exit of neuroprogenitors from the cell cycle, acting most likely in a cell-autonomous fashion.
source: In the adult brain, Notch seems to influence quiescence, cycling, and exit of neuroprogenitors from the cell cycle, acting most likely in a cell-autonomous fashion (Ables et al., 2010; Basak et al., 2012; Breunig et al., 2007; Ehm et al., 2010; Ehret et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement about adult Notch function supported by multiple citations.

claim: Glycosylation of Notch receptors by fringe proteins affects the intracellular cleavage of the heterodimeric receptor complex and generation of NICD following ligand binding.
source: Glycosylation of Notch receptors by fringe proteins affects the intracellular cleavage of the heterodimeric receptor complex and generation of the Notch1 Intra Cellular Domain (NICD) following ligand binding.
evidence: Mechanistic explanation based on established knowledge of fringe function.

claim: NICD production typically increases upon binding by Delta-like (Dll) and decreases following Jagged1 (Jag1) binding.
source: Typically, NICD production increases upon binding by Delta-like (Dll) and decreases following Jagged1 (Jag1) binding (LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005); differential Notch cleavage ensures varying expression of downstream cell cycle genes (Chapouton et al., 2010; Isomura and Kageyama, 2014; Nellemann et al., 2001; Ninov et al., 2012; Yoshiura et al., 2007).
evidence: Mechanistic explanation supported by multiple citations.

claim: Differential Notch cleavage ensures varying expression of downstream cell cycle genes.
source: Typically, NICD production increases upon binding by Delta-like (Dll) and decreases following Jagged1 (Jag1) binding (LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005); differential Notch cleavage ensures varying expression of downstream cell cycle genes (Chapouton et al., 2010; Isomura and Kageyama, 2014; Nellemann et al., 2001; Ninov et al., 2012; Yoshiura et al., 2007).
evidence: Mechanistic explanation supported by multiple citations.
